# Crash day: 4 June 2024

*Generated by `./gradlew :report:crashDay` from the files listed under [Inputs](#inputs). Do not edit by hand: change the code or the inputs and run it again.*

On 4 June 2024 India's general-election results came in well short of the exit polls. The Nifty 50 opened 0.4% down and then fell almost 9% from the open by 12:29 before recovering part of the loss; India VIX went from about 21 to 31.7. This is that day replayed, minute by minute, against a seeded book of 100,000 accounts opened at the 3 June close, through the same shard code the live engine runs.

**Time to clear** is measured in the replay's log time, the market's clock, not the laptop's. The broker in this replay fills every leg before the next minute's tick (see [What the replay assumes](#what-the-replay-assumes)), so an account's square-off takes less than a minute once started; the spread comes from accounts crossing 120% at different times of the day. Per account, start to end: median 0 min, longest 182 min (minute granularity).

### When the square-offs happened

Square-offs came in waves: the six busiest minutes hold 3,413 of the 9,060. An account is squared off on its third tick in a row at or above 120%, and the seeded thin sellers hold similar at-the-money positions at similar utilisation, so they cross together when the market takes another leg down. A real book is more varied and would spread out more.

Thinly funded short sellers started the day at 80–99% utilisation by design (decision 30); everyone else at 20–70%. Option buyers need no margin (decision 23) and cannot be margin-called; their losses stop at the premium they paid.

## The five worst accounts

Ranked by the largest margin shortfall reached during the day: required margin minus available margin, the money the account would have had to add to be covered. Equity is what the account would be worth if closed out: cash, futures profit and loss, and the value of options held net of options written. Below zero, the account has lost more than it had, and the difference is the broker's loss if the client does not pay.

## How long the engine took

Four shards, one thread each, in one process on the development laptop (Apple M4 MacBook Air), timed with `System.nanoTime()` around applying each event. This is shard compute time: there is no broker hop in this replay, so it is not the tick-to-margin figure in [results.md](results.md), which includes Redpanda.

| | Slowest shard, applying the tick | Slowest shard, applying that minute's square-off fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median minute | 4.18 ms | 0.00 ms |
| p99 minute | 26.29 ms | 0.67 ms |
| Busiest minute (10:58, 782 legs) | 26.29 ms | 0.50 ms |
| Slowest minute | 50.83 ms | 15.45 ms |

The first tick includes the JIT warming up. Timings vary between runs; the counts above do not.

| India VIX high, 4 June | 31.71 (12:30 bar high) | 31.71 | Yes |
| India VIX, 3 June close | 21.13 (15:29 bar close); 20.94 (4 June 09:15 bar open) | about 20.9 (reported −14.9% from 24.60) | The seed uses 20.94, the official close carried into the next day's first bar. |

Published figures are from press reports of NSE data (see decision 116), not from NSE's own download, which refuses scripted access. Treat the right-hand column as corroborated, not as an official extract.

The seeded book's start spot (23,320.33) is implied from the June future's settlement price by removing cost of carry (decision 30), about 56 points above the official 3 June close of 23,263.90. The first tick (09:16, 22,755.90) therefore looks 2.4% below the start, where the market had gapped 2.2%.

## What the replay assumes

- **The broker fills every square-off leg in full, at the engine's mark, before the next minute's tick.** No rejects, timeouts or duplicates (the chaos broker is tested separately: M5 gate). Real fills on 4 June came with slippage, wide spreads and some rejected orders; this replay closes positions at model prices.
- **One volatility for every strike and expiry:** VIX ÷ 100 (decision 20). Out-of-the-money options carry a higher implied volatility in the market (the smile), so short strangles look cheaper here than they were.
- **No calendar spread charge** (decision 26) and a flat 2% exposure margin: NSE adds 1.75% on calendar spreads, 3% on options more than 10% out of the money and 5% beyond nine months.
- **One price scan range for all expiries:** NSE uses 17.7% for index options more than nine months out.
- **Futures are priced from spot by cost of carry** (decision 15); the real basis on the day is ignored.
- **Margin thresholds (80 / 100 / 120%, three ticks) are a broker's policy**, guessed, not an NSE rule.
- **No user orders.** Nobody adds money, hedges or closes on their own during the day.
- **The book is synthetic.** Accounts and their positions are generated (decision 2, 30), not real clients: the counts say how this engine behaves on this book on this day, not how many Indian traders were margin-called.
- Timings are from one fanless laptop.

## Reproduce

```bash
./gradlew -q :replayer:installDist && R=replayer/build/install/replayer/bin/replayer
$R instruments --bhavcopy data/raw/fo03JUN2024bhav.csv --lots data/reference/nifty_lots_2024-06-03.csv \
               --date 2024-06-03 --out data/processed/instruments-2024-06-03.csv
$R bars --in data/raw/nifty_1min_2024-06-03_04.json --from 2024-06-03 --to 2024-06-04 --out data/processed/NIFTY-1m.csv
$R bars --in data/raw/vix_1min_2024-06-03_04.json   --from 2024-06-03 --to 2024-06-04 --out data/processed/INDIAVIX-1m.csv
$R seed --instruments data/processed/instruments-2024-06-03.csv --vix 20.94 --out data/seed --seed 42 --accounts 100000
$R ticks --bars data/processed/NIFTY-1m.csv --vix data/processed/INDIAVIX-1m.csv --from 2024-06-04 --to 2024-06-04 \
         --partitions 4 --out data/processed/logs
./gradlew :report:crashDay
```
